The cower. PURE tier 1-3: three of the six synthesised faces, whole-actor scaleBy/dy moves, one effect, one small shake, and ad-hoc `parts` transforms on `head` and `body`, both guaranteed by ToonRigRepair. No clip, no declared pose, so it casts on every rig.

The comedy is the UP before the DOWN. He startles 5% TALLER at 0.22 and hangs there for four tenths - then drops to 70% and a crouch in one move. Take the rise out and the drop reads as a glitch in the staging rather than a decision the character made. The head snaps DOWN into the shoulders and the body squashes on the same frame the eased whole-actor move begins, so the silhouette collapses hard while the position slides smooth; that mismatch is the cartoon.

Then the HOLD: from 2.15 to 2.80 there is literally nothing. Small, still, and 0.65s long. Stillness is the payoff of a shrink, and it is the beat authors always cut.

He is put back: parts released, then two eased moves home to scaleBy 1.0 on the mark, because position and scale carry to the end of the SCENE. He straightens but is left worried - expressions survive a cut.
